name: Vale of Harrow
origin: SW corner; +x east, +y north, metres; z up (metres above datum)
height_f32_row_order: row 0 = SOUTH edge (y=0); index = j*res + i, x=i*cell, y=j*cell

water.datum_note: no sea on this map; water surface = height + water depth

layers.height.f32: float32 LE terrain/bed height (m), south-first rows
layers.water.f32: float32 LE water depth (m), south-first rows (js/sim/map.js loads this)
layers.river_flow.png: uint8 log10 upstream area; 255 = main river channel
layers.surface.u8: uint8 surface id (index into surfaceKeys), south-first rows, res x res
layers.canopy.u8: uint8 canopy / tall-vegetation height in metres above ground, south-first rows
layers.vegetation.json: tree & shrub instances {asset,x,y,rot,scale} in world metres

features.name: Ashby (blue town)
features.note: Blue home plateau: flat, dry, 3 approaches; SW corner has only farmland behind it.

features.name: Rookham (red town)
features.note: Red home plateau on higher ground; the Gallows Gap and the Knap screen its southern approaches.

features.name: Harrow Ridge
features.note: Dominant ridge: steep NW forward face over the bridge, long reverse slope SE hides troops from the red bank.

features.name: Harrow Ridge reverse slope
features.note: Dead ground to anyone north of the river: form up and reserve here unseen.

features.name: Tor Knap (ruin)
features.note: Steep isolated hill with a flat summit and ruin; commands the bridge and marsh, hard to storm, easy to isolate.

features.name: River Harrow
features.note: Unfordable (1.7-2.3 m) except at the fords; flows W edge to S edge.

features.name: Hob's Ford
features.note: Wide gravel riffle ~0.4 m deep; western crossing, overlooked by Blackfell scree.

features.name: Stane Ford
features.note: Eastern gravel riffle ~0.4 m deep; links Harrow Field to the Gallows Gap.

features.name: Harrow Bridge site
features.note: Narrow deep reach with firm raised banks: the only place to bridge; the centre of the map.

features.name: Harrow Moss
features.note: Floodplain marsh inside the bend below the bridge: infantry wade, cavalry and guns bog down.

features.name: Gallows Gap
features.note: Narrow pass between Brant Hill and Cold Knowe: a column is trapped; a few can hold it.

features.name: Brant Hill
features.note: West jaw of the Gap; steep inner face.

features.name: Cold Knowe
features.note: East jaw of the Gap; steep inner face.

features.name: Harrow Field
features.note: Long gentle open plain, <3 deg: ideal cavalry ground behind the ridge's reverse slope.

features.name: Wychwood Bottom
features.note: Steep-sided tributary valley (intended woodland): a covered approach from Ashby to Hob's Ford.

features.name: Crake Gill
features.note: Deep narrow stream gully draining the mere: covered route and obstacle just upstream of the bridge.

features.name: Harrow Mere
features.note: Lake, level 89.49 m, up to ~8 m deep: anchors a flank, impassable.

features.name: Blackfell
features.note: Rocky upland with crags and scree aprons: slow going, superb observation over the western river.

features.name: Holloway (sunken lane)
features.note: Lane worn 3 m into the slope: ready-made trench and covered approach to the bridge.

features.name: Rook Beck
features.note: Shallow beck valley past Rookham to the river: a low covered line of approach toward the Knap.

features.name: Hanger Knoll
features.note: Small rounded knoll (intended woodland): observation post and screen west of Rookham.

features.name: Ashby farmland
features.note: Rolling fields, hedge-scale undulation: partial cover for infantry.

features.name: Rookham farmland
features.note: Rolling fields around Rookham on a gentle south-facing slope.
